caseName: Natural Resources Defense Council, Inc. v. U.S. Department of the Interior
court: U.S. District Court, Southern District of New York
penalty: Not applicable: administrative judicial review, not a criminal animal count.
followup: Appeal dismissed March 2, 2021 at government's request; 2025 DOI memorandum preserves an SDNY exception.
limitations: Selected precedent; no prosecution, animal total, or national case census.

caseName: United States v. Robert J. Stevens
court: Supreme Court of the United States; underlying W.D. Pennsylvania
disposition: Three trial convictions were vacated by the Third Circuit; Supreme Court affirmed invalidation.
penalty: Original concurrent 37-month sentences and three years' supervised release were attached to the vacated convictions.
followup: 2010 replacement statute enacted; this case is a failed conviction, not a successful enforcement outcome.
limitations: Animal suffering prevented cannot be inferred; sale-of-depictions prosecution, not a conviction for the underlying fights.

court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit; underlying S.D. Texas
disposition: Three video-related convictions affirmed; one video-creation conviction vacated with judgment of acquittal.
penalty: 57-month concurrent terms; opinion reports 14 months after credit for related state custody.
followup: No resentencing required after reversal of one count; opinion is unpublished.
limitations: Do not report all four original convictions as upheld, combine federal/state penalties, or treat sentence as an animal-welfare outcome.

caseName: United States v. Odell S. Anderson, Sr.
court: U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia
disposition: Guilty plea to dogfighting conspiracy and causing a child under 16 to attend.
penalty: 18 months on each count, concurrently; three years' supervised release.
followup: Agency reports sentence; completion, recidivism, and animal placement not established.
limitations: Bulletin gives Nos.3:21-CR-00023–00026 for multi-defendant group without mapping a specific docket to Anderson; left null. Do not add the concurrent terms.

caseName: United States v. Krystal Cherika Scott
court: U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana
disposition: Found guilty; sentenced for animal crushing.
penalty: DOJ reports 30 months' imprisonment and five years' supervised release.
followup: Release was updated February 26, 2024; no independently retrieved post-sentence record.
limitations: Date denotes sentencing-report publication. Judgment not obtained, including verification of reported supervised-release term. Exact number of animals not supplied.

caseName: United States v. Kenneth J. Herrera
court: U.S. District Court for the Western District of Wisconsin
statute: 18 U.S.C. §48 video provisions; release describes PACT Act
disposition: Guilty plea for creating, selling and distributing an animal-crushing video, as described by DOJ.
penalty: 12 months and one day imprisonment; three years' supervised release; $5,000 fine.
followup: No completed supervision or recidivism outcome retrieved.
limitations: One monkey is described in the charged video, not a total case-victim census. A video case cannot establish incremental effect of PACT's new conduct offense.

caseName: United States v. Samuel Alexander Gray
court: U.S. District Court for the District of South Carolina
statute: Animal-fighting venture and felon-in-possession offenses; release omits exact statutory subsections
penalty: 15 months imprisonment; three years' supervision with no dog ownership.
followup: Dogs were seized following September 2023 investigation; final animal disposition not reported.
limitations: Date denotes sentencing-report publication. Mixed firearm/fighting sentence cannot be attributed solely to animal-fighting law. Fourteen denotes seized dogs, not all harmed animals.

caseName: United States v. Desmond Levon Brown
court: U.S. District Court for the District of South Carolina
statute: 18 U.S.C. §48 animal-crushing offense; release labels prosecution under PACT
disposition: Sentence reported for purposeful killing of a puppy by burning.
penalty: 60 months imprisonment; three years' supervision prohibiting animal ownership or possession.
followup: Latest reviewed report October 15, 2026; appeal and sentence completion unknown.
limitations: Date is release date, not independently verified judgment date. Agency's 'first PACT case' claim applies to South Carolina district, not the nation.

caseName: Humane Society of the United States v. United States Department of Agriculture
court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit
statute: Administrative Procedure Act; Horse Protection Act rulemaking
disposition: Reversed and remanded; withdrawal of a rule made available for public inspection required notice and comment.
penalty: No criminal sentence or animal-count finding; regulatory judicial review.
followup: USDA conducted notice-and-comment withdrawal in 2023 and finalized a replacement rule in 2024.
limitations: Procedural decision, not a conviction or measured reduction in soring.

caseName: Tennessee Walking Horse National Celebration Association et al. v. United States Department of Agriculture et al.
court: U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas
statute: Horse Protection Act; Administrative Procedure Act
disposition: Partly vacated the 2024 rule, including specified equipment/substance prohibitions, dermatologic criteria and review provisions; inspector-system replacement survived.
followup: USDA's January 2026 rule postponed the main non-vacated amendments until December 31, 2026; §11.19 training authorization was already effective June 7, 2024.
limitations: Disposition verified through USDA's subsequent Federal Register account; district-court opinion was not independently retrieved. Do not count as animal-cruelty enforcement.

caseName: Humane Society of the United States et al. v. National Institutes of Health et al.
court: U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland
disposition: Vacated NIH's Alamogordo transfer-ineligibility decision and remanded; required compliance with statutory sanctuary acceptance.
followup: Chimp Haven reports receiving all remaining Alamogordo chimpanzees in 2025; individual transfer records not audited here.
limitations: Civil judicial review, not animal-cruelty prosecution. No assumption that court alone caused later transfers.
